strategy.summary: Reproduce NumPy issue #29372 by running the added regression tests in numpy/lib/tests/test_arraysetops.py against the buggy revision bde097d548a1 and verifying that np.unique(..., equal_nan=True) fails to collapse NaNs for 1D inputs (axis=0 or axis=-1). The fixed revision should pass by treating NaNs as equal in the 1D/axis special-case.

build_commands: python -m pip install -U pip setuptools wheel
pinned_because: No version constraints are provided in the evidence (unbounded). The only hard requirement to transition buggy->fixed is checking out the specified buggy commit bde097d548a1 and then the PR-fixed revision.
Pytest/hypothesis are required to run the test suite; their versions are not pinned by the evidence.

strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision (bde097d548a1), the regression assertion assert_array_equal(result, expected) fails because np.unique(np.array([np.nan, 0, 0, np.nan]), axis=0, equal_nan=True) does NOT collapse NaNs into a single unique value for 1D inputs. On the fixed revision for PR #29372, the same test passes because np.unique(..., equal_nan=True) treats NaNs as equal in the 1D/axis special-case and returns [0., np.nan].
strategy.numerical_probe: Use the regression test input arr1d = np.array([np.nan, 0, 0, np.nan]) with equal_nan=True and axis=0 (and axis=-1). Do not add extra numeric inspection; rely on assert_array_equal in the test.
risks: The evidence does not specify exact Python/NumPy build flags, compiler, or architecture; the transition could be sensitive to how NumPy is built. Use a standard local editable build (pip install -e .) on the same machine for both buggy and fixed revisions.
The provided tests cover only the 1D case (ar.ndim==1) with axis=0 and axis=-1; do not generalize to 2D/other axis values for this reproduction.
The evidence mentions only NaN behavior; other special values (inf, -inf, signed zero) are not part of this regression and are not required for the test to pass/fail.

oracle.reference_source: The regression tests shown in the provided diff (assert_array_equal against expected=np.array([0., np.nan])).
oracle.why: The test uses assert_array_equal with strict array equality for the returned unique set ordering/contents.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The assertion assert_array_equal(result, expected) fails in test_unique_axis0_equal_nan_on_1d_array (and test_unique_axis_minus1_eq_on_1d_array) because np.unique does not treat NaNs as equal for 1D inputs when equal_nan=True, so the output contains both NaNs (i.e., the unique result does not equal np.array([0., np.nan])).
strategy.passes_on_fixed: The same assertions pass because the fix routes the 1D/axis special-case through _unique1d with equal_nan=equal_nan, causing NaNs to be treated as equal and collapsed to a single np.nan in the unique output.
